newsitem.title: POLAND: GYPSIES CONDEMN NATIONALISM AT AUSCHWITZ MEMORIAL.
newsitem.headline: GYPSIES CONDEMN NATIONALISM AT AUSCHWITZ MEMORIAL.

text.p: Gypsies from across Europe gathered at the former Auschwitz-Birkenau death camp complex on Saturday to condemn nationalism and mourn the mass murder of Roma people by Nazi Germans during World War Two.

The annual ceremony specifically recalls the gassing on the night of August 2, 1944, of about 3,000 Gypsy prisoners -- largely women and children -- who had survived in a special compound of the extermination complex in southern Poland.
It also commemorates the many hundreds of thousands of Gypsies killed elsewhere by the Nazis in what some commentators call a "forgotten Holocaust".

About 100 members of communities from countries including Germany, Serbia, Romania, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland as well as Australia walked quietly to a memorial amid the foundations of Birkenau's Block 28, where Gypsies were held.

In steady rain new memorial plaques to the dead were placed and Roman Rose, the head of the central council of Roma in Germany, reminded the gathering of a recent European Union report discussing a breach of minority rights in the neighbouring Czech Republic and Hungary.
"I appeal that this type of practice be eliminated and that nationalism not be able to spawn into the National Socialism which led to the fascist occupation," he said.

Gypsy leaders in Poland have noted the difficulty of establishing exactly how many Gypsies were murdered during the war as many were just shot wherever the Germans found them along roadsides or in woods.
Up to 1.5 million people, most of them Jews, were murdered at Auschwitz-Birkenau, which is now preserved as a museum.
